speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. I understand you are experiencing generalized fatigue and severe itching, along with abnormal liver function tests. Can you tell me if you have noticed any yellowing of your skin or eyes, or any changes in the color of your urine or stools?

speaker: Patient
text: 32-year-old male. The patient reports a 2-month history of increasing generalized fatigue and severe pruritus. He has known hypertension and was diagnosed with ulcerative colitis 5 years ago. He mentions being sexually active with 2 female partners and inconsistent condom use.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of ulcerative colitis, I need to rule out Primary Sclerosing Cholangitis, but your sexual history raises concern for viral hepatitis. Have you experienced any dark urine, pale stools, or right upper quadrant abdominal pain?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Generalized fatigue and severe pruritus. I also have Scleral icterus, Multiple scratch marks on trunk and extremities.

speaker: Doctor
text: To help differentiate between viral hepatitis and cholestatic diseases, have you noticed any dark urine or pale, clay-colored stools? Additionally, do you consume alcohol regularly or take any herbal supplements?

speaker: Doctor
text: I am concerned about Primary Biliary Cholangitis, so I need to check for specific antibodies. REQUEST TEST: Antimitochondrial Antibodies (AMA)

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the negative AMA and the strong association with ulcerative colitis, I suspect microscopic cholangitis or early PSC not yet visible on MRCP. REQUEST TEST: Liver Biopsy

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the patient's young age, male gender, history of ulcerative colitis, and severe pruritus with cholestatic liver enzymes but normal MRCP, biopsy, and AMA, this presentation is highly suggestive of small-duct Primary Sclerosing Cholangitis or an atypical autoimmune cholestatic condition often seen in UC patients. DIAGNOSIS READY: Small-duct Primary Sclerosing Cholangitis
